criteria.rationale: The assumption that listing the changed specs is enough to check their transitions is false below the repository top. L1 was read and is not disputed.
The change adds no shared mutable state in production; memfdWrite is a test seam restored by its test. Index lookup deadlines are unchanged; L1 covers the ledger one.
A root below the top that passed check can now fail on a spec that did not transition.

--relative, TruncateUTF8 and the failing untracked listing address their causes. The redaction design (substring replacement before the generic pattern) causes N2 and N3. The design assessment observed no structural deltas.

Examined the spec API/contract section and searched docs-site/docs/cli.md: it states the validate command line but nothing about redaction or listing failure that this change contradicts. The spec states the new selection failure.
The failed untracked listing names the range, the command and the Git message in English, the CLI exits 2 and carry reports the selection as unused. Focused test passed.
The eight code files in the range match the spec artifact list and R1-R5; no unrelated behaviour was added. N7 is outside this scope.
Replacing known directories is a small design, but without path-boundary handling it is not sufficient: it removes relative text and keeps absolute tails.

findings.action: R1 is incomplete: with the root below the repository top the new --relative candidates reach `git show HEAD:<root-relative path>`, which Git resolves from the top. The old text comes back empty, so a modified spec already in-progress at HEAD and not ready fails strict check as a new transition (reproduced). A same-named spec at the top would be read instead and could hide a real transition (by reading). The R1 test checks only the candidate list.

Regression: replacing known directories as bare substrings leaves the tail of other paths in the versioned report, because the generic pattern no longer matches after <path>. Reproduced with HOME=/home/jane: /home/jane/clients/acme-secret/index gives <path>/clients/acme-secret/index, /home/janet/x gives <path>t/x, and <root>-acme-secret/index gives <path>-acme-secret/index. The base pattern removed these unspaced paths whole.

Known directories are also replaced inside relative names: with TMPDIR=/tmp, feature/tmp-cleanup becomes feature<path>-cleanup, and docs/home/jane/notes becomes docs<path>/notes (reproduced). Relative names were kept before.

R2 is not met outside the known directories: `open /mnt/jane doe/index` becomes `open <path> doe/index` (reproduced). Spaces, quotes or parentheses still cut the match, while the spec marks R2 satisfied. The test input [/srv/x y] asserts only that /srv is gone, not the tail.

By reading, not run on Windows: filepath.Clean turns known directories into backslash form, while Git prints forward slashes, so the whole-directory replacement would not match paths in Git messages there.
The leading-colon case of R2 has no failing test: with `:` removed from the prefix class, TestTheReportRemovesWholePaths and the other report tests run still pass (mutation by test overlay).

Pre-existing and outside R1-R5: with the root below the repository top, the scope diff lists top-relative paths (no --relative) while ls-files lists root-relative ones. A changed file in a self-contained module is then owned by no module and the module is not selected: changed=[proj/mod/x.txt], selected empty, no error (reproduced). Validation narrows silently.
